tagline: A deterministic, no_std Minesweeper state machine shaped for reinforcement learning.
short_description: An allocation-free 8x8 Minesweeper engine with seeded SplitMix64 boards, observation/action-mask tensors, configurable strikes, and a browser conformance harness.
long_description: mine-sm packages Minesweeper as a tiny reinforcement-learning environment rather than a game. The no_std Rust crate uses a flat 64-cell bitboard with no heap and exposes a three-call API: build a board from a seed or an exact mine mask, apply Reveal/Flag actions, and read back a [f32; 64] observation plus a legal-action mask shaped for a neural network. Bomb placement uses a hand-rolled SplitMix64 PRNG and rejection sampling, so the same (seed, actions) sequence produces byte-identical games on Wasm and native x86/ARM. Rules are configurable between classic sudden death and multi-strike/shielded play, and the engine implements safe first reveal, zero-cell cascade, flag protection, and terminal-state masking. The live harness visualizes observations and masks, auto-plays winning and losing lines, and runs conformance checks against the Rust engine; the repo includes golden, proptest, and scenario suites plus a quickstart example and ONNX-policy-friendly tooling.
notes: Custom domain mines-sm.livive.net from CNAME; GitHub Pages also serves the repo path. The importable crate is named mine-sm (module mine_sm), while the repo and listing key are mines-sm. Dual-licensed MIT/Apache-2.0. Distinct from the mines-livive-net arcade game: this is the headless RL environment and conformance harness.

how_to_play.title: 1. Step the environment
how_to_play.body: Reveal or flag cells on a seeded 8x8 board. The harness shows the engine's observation encoding (-1 hidden, -0.5 flagged, -2 detonated, 0.0-0.8 adjacency) and the action mask returned to an agent.

how_to_play.title: 2. Change the rules
how_to_play.body: Switch between classic sudden death and multi-strike shielded play, then auto-play a winning or losing line to see how strikes and terminal masking behave.

how_to_play.title: 3. Verify determinism
how_to_play.body: Run the built-in conformance checks against the Rust engine. Identical seeds and action sequences reproduce identical boards across Wasm and native targets.
